items.title: Locally bounded distributional weak solutions of scalar laws
items.statement: A locally bounded distributional weak formulation with the initial boundary term; it extends the published bounded definition only by allowing locally bounded states.
items.strategy: Define the local essential-bound condition and weak identity for tests that may meet t=0.

references.title: H. De Sterck and P. Ullrich, Introduction to Computational PDEs, Chapter 3, complete chapter, PDF pp. 81–106
references.locator: §3.2.1, pp. 83–84, and §3.2.3, pp. 88–90: scalar conservation laws, integral balances and weak shocks.

references.title: Gregory A. Chechkin and Andrey Yu. Goritsky, S. N. Kruzhkov’s lectures on first-order quasilinear PDEs, complete lecture notes in Analytical and Numerical Aspects of PDEs (de Gruyter, 2009)
references.locator: Complete 67-page lecture notes; §4.1, equation (4.3), PDF p. 19 (printed p. 19): compactly supported test-function weak integral identity for the scalar conservation law.

items.title: Conservative two-point finite-volume schemes for scalar laws
items.statement: A uniform-grid two-point conservative update with cell-average initial data and a continuous diagonal-consistent numerical flux.
items.strategy: Specify full-line cells, cell-average initialization, one shared face flux and the conservative flux-difference update.

references.title: H. De Sterck and P. Ullrich, Introduction to Computational PDEs, Chapter 3, complete chapter, PDF pp. 81–106
references.locator: §3.4.1, PDF pp. 94–96: cell averages, shared numerical face fluxes, update and the diagonal consistency condition; §3.4.3, pp. 97–99: cancellation of interior face fluxes.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Lecture 19: Finite Volume Methods, complete six-page note
references.locator: pp. 1–2: cell-average states, finite-volume update, Godunov reconstruction/evolution/averaging and the local Riemann problem.

items.title: Piecewise-constant finite-volume state and face-flux reconstructions
items.statement: Piecewise-constant state and face-flux reconstructions on each space-time cell, with face flux equal to F(U_j,U_{j+1}).
items.strategy: Define both reconstructions from the scheme and fix null-boundary conventions.

references.title: H. De Sterck and P. Ullrich, Introduction to Computational PDEs, Chapter 3, complete chapter, PDF pp. 81–106
references.locator: §3.4.1, pp. 94–96: cell averages, fluxes over time slabs and the space-time finite-volume grid.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Lecture 19: Finite Volume Methods, complete six-page note
references.locator: p. 1: a finite-volume value is the cell average and the scheme balances fluxes through cell boundaries.

items.title: Godunov numerical flux for Burgers' equation
items.statement: The explicit two-state Godunov flux for convex Burgers flux f_B(s)=s^2/2.
items.strategy: Give deterministic case formulas for increasing and decreasing states.

references.title: H. De Sterck and P. Ullrich, Introduction to Computational PDEs, Chapter 3, complete chapter, PDF pp. 81–106
references.locator: §3.2.3 and §3.4.1, pp. 88–89 and 94–96: Burgers flux, shock speed, and the two-state numerical flux interface.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Lecture 19: Finite Volume Methods, complete six-page note
references.locator: pp. 1–2: Burgers equation, Godunov reconstruction/evolution/averaging and the local Riemann problem.

items.title: The Burgers Godunov flux is continuous and consistent
items.statement: The Burgers Godunov flux is continuous on R^2 and satisfies G(a,a)=f_B(a).
items.strategy: Check continuity on open branches and switching boundaries, then verify the diagonal.

references.title: H. De Sterck and P. Ullrich, Introduction to Computational PDEs, Chapter 3, complete chapter, PDF pp. 81–106
references.locator: §3.4.1, pp. 94–96: the numerical flux has the diagonal consistency condition; §3.4.2, pp. 96–97: a scalar numerical flux is specified on pairs of states.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Lecture 19: Finite Volume Methods, complete six-page note
references.locator: pp. 1–2: Godunov construction for Burgers states.

items.title: Discrete weak identity for a conservative finite-volume update
items.statement: Testing the conservative update by space-time cell averages gives the exact discrete weak identity.
items.strategy: Multiply the update, telescope in time, reindex shared face fluxes in space, and retain the initial cell term.

references.title: H. De Sterck and P. Ullrich, Introduction to Computational PDEs, Chapter 3, complete chapter, PDF pp. 81–106
references.locator: §3.4.1 and §3.4.3, pp. 94–99: cell-average updates, shared interface fluxes and cancellation of interior fluxes.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Lecture 19: Finite Volume Methods, complete six-page note
references.locator: p. 1: finite-volume cell averages and the conservative flux-difference update.

items.title: Strong local convergence of consistent finite-volume face fluxes
items.statement: Under local uniform boundedness and strong local L1 convergence, continuous consistent face-flux reconstructions converge locally to f(u).
items.strategy: Use spatial translation continuity, continuity on compact state ranges, and local control of the initial strip.
items.axiom_base: Assume only the Axiom of Countable Choice ACω, used in step 2.1 through the published L1 translation-continuity theorem for a compactly supported cutoff. No dependent or arbitrary-index choice is used.

references.title: H. De Sterck and P. Ullrich, Introduction to Computational PDEs, Chapter 3, complete chapter, PDF pp. 81–106
references.locator: §3.4.1, pp. 94–96: consistent two-state numerical fluxes and face updates; the local convergence argument is supplied here.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Lecture 19: Finite Volume Methods, complete six-page note
references.locator: pp. 1–2: two-state numerical face fluxes; the L1 passage is proved locally using the declared published translation-continuity interface.

items.title: Conservative finite-volume strong-limit theorem
items.statement: Strong local L1 convergence and local uniform state bounds for a conservative consistent two-point scheme imply the limit satisfies the distributional weak identity with cell-average initial data.
items.strategy: Use discrete summation by parts, test-function quadrature estimates, strong state/face-flux convergence, and the initial boundary term; compactness and entropy are not conclusions.
items.axiom_base: Assume ACω, inherited only for the local spatial-translation step in the face-flux convergence lemma. The cellwise summation and passage to the weak identity use no further choice.

references.title: H. De Sterck and P. Ullrich, Introduction to Computational PDEs, Chapter 3, complete chapter, PDF pp. 81–106
references.locator: §3.4.1 and §3.4.3, pp. 94–99: conservative cell updates and interior-flux cancellation; Theorem 3.1 on pp. 98–99 states a Lax–Wendroff conclusion without the compactness and bounded-range hypotheses or a proof. The complete conditional proof is supplied locally.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Lecture 19: Finite Volume Methods, complete six-page note
references.locator: pp. 1–2: cell-average states, conservative update and Godunov flux construction; the conditional weak-limit proof is supplied locally.

items.title: Godunov finite volumes preserve the Burgers shock speed
items.statement: The Burgers Godunov update exactly preserves the stationary 1-to−1 shock, whose Rankine–Hugoniot speed is zero.
items.strategy: Evaluate interface fluxes, show the update is stationary, verify the weak identity directly, and compute the jump speed.

references.title: H. De Sterck and P. Ullrich, Introduction to Computational PDEs, Chapter 3, complete chapter, PDF pp. 81–106
references.locator: §3.2.3 and §§3.4.1–3.4.3, pp. 88–99: Burgers shock speed, cell-average updates, Godunov fluxes and conservation.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Lecture 19: Finite Volume Methods, complete six-page note
references.locator: pp. 1–2: Burgers Godunov method and shock-wave Riemann problems.

items.title: Uniformly bounded cell reconstructions need not have a strong local limit
items.statement: A dyadic sequence of uniformly bounded alternating cell reconstructions has no strongly L1loc-convergent subsequence.
items.strategy: Show pairwise L1 separation on one compact space-time rectangle; no update trajectory is asserted.

items.title: A conservative consistent finite-volume weak limit need not be entropic
items.statement: The Burgers Godunov update with tau/h=2 has a strongly convergent bounded expansion-shock limit that is weak but not Kruzhkov entropic.
items.strategy: Prove the exact one-cell shift, local L1 convergence, weak limit, and direct entropy-inequality violation; the CFL condition fails.
items.axiom_base: Assume ACω, as required by the weak-limit and L1-translation suppliers; the entropy-defect calculation uses no further choice.

references.title: H. De Sterck and P. Ullrich, Introduction to Computational PDEs, Chapter 3, complete chapter, PDF pp. 81–106
references.locator: §3.2.3 and §3.4, pp. 88–99: Rankine–Hugoniot speed and conservative finite-volume updates; the entropy-violating sequence is proved locally.

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Lecture 19: Finite Volume Methods, complete six-page note
references.locator: pp. 1–2: Godunov flux and conservative cell update; the CFL-violating trajectory and entropy defect are verified locally.
